description_full: United Bankshares, Inc., through its subsidiaries, provides commercial and retail banking products and services in the United States. The company accepts checking, savings, and time and money market accounts; individual retirement accounts; and demand deposits, statement and special savings, and NOW accounts. Its loan products include commercial loans and leases to small to mid-size industrial and commercial companies, as well as automobile dealers, service, retail and wholesale merchants; construction and real estate loans, such as commercial and residential mortgages, and loans secured by owner-occupied real estate; personal, automobiles, boats, recreational vehicles, credit card receivables, commercial, and floor plan loans; and home equity loans. In addition, the company provides credit cards; trust, safe deposit boxes, wire transfers, and other banking products and services; investment and security services; buying and selling federal fund services; automated teller machine services; and internet and automated telephone banking services. Further, it offers community banking services, such as asset management, real property title insurance, financial planning, mortgage banking, and brokerage services, as well as custody of assets, investment management, escrow services, and related fiduciary activities. The company was incorporated in 1982 and is headquartered in Charleston, West Virginia.

financial_summary: United Bankshares, Inc. is a mid-cap financial services business with a $6.2B market cap on $1.2B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +6% over the past three years and +10% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 6% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.

The business throws off $481M in free cash flow — roughly 39 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.07× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.2× net debt/EBITDA, and thin 1.0× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 5.4% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 2.2% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 1.8× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 37% over the past year excluding the latest month.

The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 16%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $40.78 to $70.54 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.

prof: ROIC of 6% falls short of the cost of capital of 9.1%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.56).

own: Insiders own a modest 2.2%, and institutions hold 78%.
It returns 5.4% a year to shareholders (2.0% in buybacks and 3.3% in dividends).

people: With about 2,812 employees, each generates about $440K of revenue, in line with the Financial Services median, and revenue has grown 9.9% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $171K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $3.4M (8x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (1/10, lower is better).
